agenda_text:
CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
June 2, 2021 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s  Executive  Order  N-29-20(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf), please note that
members of the public will only be allowed to observe and address
the Planning Commission Meeting of June 2, 2021 at 7:00 P.M. by
telephone, video and other electronic means, as follows:

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited
  video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/
   The above access options provide the public with the
  opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting.
   However, members of the public who wish to orally address the
  Planning Commission must use the public access options noted
  below:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Dial-in: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 9452091# wait 2 seconds and press # again

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:

    When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
    If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an
  area with good reception.
    If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute
  the sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from
  the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making
  public comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to
Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members
of the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda,
comments must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on June 2, 2021, the
day of the meeting. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date
and agenda item. Comments received after 12:00 P.M. and prior to
close of the public hearing will be made part of the official public
record of the meeting.
[Agenda Items and Additional Public Access Options Listed on
Following Pages]
 1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other
  than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Bernadette
  Rodriguez, representing B. Rodriguez Permanent Makeup, for
  Special Use Permit No. 2021-004 (SP-2021-004) to allow: 1)
  a beauty salon, within 300 feet of a similar use; and 2) a
  tattoo parlor (for permanent make-up) within an existing
  multi-tenant commercial building on an approximately 5,000
  square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at
  8410 South 8th Avenue.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm the categorical exemption EA-CE-2021-028; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2021-004,
  subject to 16 conditions, and/or add conditions as
  deemed appropriate.

  b. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2021-001
  (ZCA-2021-001) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal
  Code to modify regulations for Smoke Shops. (This item has
  been pulled and will be re-noticed)

  c. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2021-002
  (ZCA-2021-002) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal
  Code to modify signage regulations for banners in the Public
  Right-of Way.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2021-043; and
  2) Adopt a resolution recommending City Council adoption
  of Zoning Code Amendment ZCA-2021-002.

  d. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2021-004
  (ZCA-2021-004) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal
  Code to establish regulations for Hookah Lounges. (This
  item has been pulled and will be re-noticed)

6.  NON - PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A non-public hearing to consider an application by John
  Dodson, representing Popeye’s, for Design Review No. 2021-
  002 (DR-2021-002) to approve exterior modifications and
  signs affixed to the tower element of an existing commercial
  building located within the Art Deco Overlay on an
  approximately 12,000 square-foot C-2 (General Commercial)
  zoned property at 2934 West Manchester Boulevard.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Notice of Exemption EA-CE-2021-027; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving DR-2021-002
  subject to 10 conditions, and/or add conditions as
  deemed appropriate.

7.  Commission Initiatives.

8.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

  2
 9.  Adjournment.

If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability,
please contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230, One
Manchester Boulevard, Fourth Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood,
CA 90301. All requests for special accommodations must be received
48 hours prior to the day of the hearing(s). "Si no entiende esta
noticia o si necesita más información, favor de llamar a este número
(310) 412-5230."

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of June 2, 2021
is not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other
agenda item being considered, the public hearing or non-public
hearing agenda item will automatically be continued to the next
regular Planning Commission meeting.

Hearing  materials  are  available  at
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-4
and at City Hall, 1st Floor Lobby Information Desk during regular
business hours. If any additional documents are received for
distribution to the Planning Commission after publication of this
Agenda but before 12:00 P.M. on the day of the meeting, they will
be made available for public inspection at the following webpage
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-
4.

(Note: The above procedures are subject to change for future
Commission meetings. Please refer to future Planning Commission
agendas for public participation option procedures at that time.)

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 2, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, June 2, 2021, in the City Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Patricia Patrick, the meeting was
called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
Excused
Absence: Commissioner David Rice
  Mindy Wilcox, Planning Manager

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECD Director
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Sr. Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Sr. Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Jeff Lewis, Acting Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Mr. Christopher Jackson, Sr., in regards to the Commissioner
Trejo’s Initiatives from last month’s Planning Commission Meeting,
1244 Inglewood Avenue, at the corner of Century Boulevard and
Inglewood Avenue, the Code Enforcement Division has cited the
property owner and the area was cleared of all non-working
vehicles. Code Enforcement Manager stated that Code Enforcement
staff will continue to check in with the owner to ensure the site
will stay clean.

Commissioner David Rice contacted staff and has an excused absence
and will not be attending tonight’s planning commission meeting.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None, confirmed by the AT&T Operator.

(5) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

5A: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-004 (SP-2021-004) 8410 SOUTH 8TH
AVENUE.
A public hearing to consider an application by Bernadette Rodriguez,
representing B. Rodriguez Permanent Makeup, for Special Use Permit No.
2021-004 (SP-2021-004) to allow: 1) A beauty salon, within 300 feet of
a similar use; and 2) A tattoo parlor (for permanent make-up) within an
existing multi-tenant commercial building on an approximately 5,000
square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 8410 South 8th
Avenue.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 What constitutes over concentration in the area?
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 2, 2021

   Ms. Fewell stated more than three salons within 300 feet of
  each other is what staff uses as a guideline.
   Mr. Jackson also explained to the planning commission what
  the issues are regarding this item.
  A question regarding insuring no body-piercing be allowed at
  the site, and to insure this with a condition for approval.
  - Ms. Fewell stated a condition will work.

Chairman Springs asked staff:
 Where are the other salons in the area?
   Ms. Fewell displayed all of the salons in the area.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to address the Planning
Commission and speak about their project.

Ms. Bernadette Rodriguez, spoke to the Planning Commission via
telephone regarding her project at 8410 South 8th Avenue.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant:
 Questions regarding Micro-blading and if there will be tattooing
  of eyelashes or eye-lining.
   Ms. Rodriguez explained the process of Micro-blading and
  tattooing of eyelashes and eye-lining.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant:
 Several questions regarding her project, and  the  hours  of
  operation.
   Ms. Rodriguez stated from 10:00am to 6:00pm.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant:
 Several questions regarding her project, and all safety
  precautions for the patrons.
  - Ms. Rodriguez explained her years of experience.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant:
 What is the duration of the procedure on her patrons?
   Ms. Rodriguez explained the procedure to the planning
  commission.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
The AT&T Operator opened the phone lines

1. Ms. Anirizwi – For
2. Natasha LeDay – For, also wanted it known she sent an email
  to the planning division to request the approval of this
  item.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any
final comments from the commissioners?

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated that she is very excited for
this project to come to Inglewood.

Chairman Springs called for a motion.

  2

June 2, 2021

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to affirm the
categorical exemption EA-CE-2021-028 and adopt the attached
resolution approving SP-2021-004, subject to 16 conditions, and
the added condition of no body piercing and no hair or nail
services and was seconded by Commissioner Trejo, that Resolution
No. 1897;

5C. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2021-002 (ZCA-2021-002) CHAPTER 12
IMC: A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2020-001
(ZCA-2021-002) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code to
modify signage regulations for banners in the Public Right-of Way.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff:
 Please explain the difference between a sign and a banner?
   Mr. McCrumby stated a banner is a type of temporary signage
  that has a tendency to become weathered, tattered and in need
  of replacement due to the duration it has been displayed,
  whereas a sign is mounted on a building permanently, can
  handle the elements, and generally has some sort of back-
  lighting for visibility purposes.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 Clarifying the present zoning use and what its purpose initially
  is set to do is now being changed by planning to remove the
  strict regulations?
   Mr. McCrumby stated that is correct. Currently in the City’s
  sign regulations, there is a strict prohibition of any private
  businesses or entity advertising signage on any street lights
  or in the right of way, so in order to remove that conflict
  with our Municipal Code, we need to change the regulations.

  So, planning is not inserting any language or allowing the
  potential for any political signage that may come up later in

   Mr. McCrumby stated that the project and parameters that are
  set in place would require applicants to meet certain
  criteria, for example there has to be a one-day event that
